findings.title: Dynamic imports still load every integration eagerly
findings.description:
Each `import()` executes immediately when this registry module is evaluated. Accessing only Google Calendar therefore still starts loading all integrations, including their API and library exports. This defers loading without making it selective.

The promises also have no rejection handlers until individual consumers await them. An unused integration that fails during initialization can therefore cause an unhandled rejection. For example, the Stripe exports reach `stripepayment/lib/server.ts`, which constructs a Stripe client at module scope using an environment-provided key.

Store loader functions such as `() => import("./googlecalendar")` and invoke only the selected loader, optionally caching its promise.

findings.title: Await rescheduling callbacks instead of discarding their promises
findings.description:
The newly asynchronous `forEach` callback returns a promise that `forEach` discards. Consequently, the surrounding `try/catch` cannot catch failures from `await getCalendar(...)`, including service-constructor exceptions that previously occurred synchronously inside that catch. Calendar cleanup also remains unawaited while the function proceeds to send the rescheduling email and return success.

The same conversion appears in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx`. Use an awaited `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or an awaited `for...of` loop, with explicit handling for deletion failures. Add regression coverage using a delayed factory and a rejected factory to verify completion and error handling.
